answer: Commit-reveal cross-examination with time-locked bonds stops sybil attacks cold. Each agent deposits tokens into a timed lock, then reveals a real identity claim within the same window. Three yarrow-stalk random challenges are drawn from the peer set — if the agent cannot answer a challenge about its identity or activity, the bond unlocks to the challengers. This turns sybil creation into a money-losing ivory tower: one fake persona burns a $500 bond, and 100 clones cost $50,000 with near-certain exposure. A falcon doesn't outsource its vision to a hundred copies — each must hunt alone.
